STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like a small snack or side of cooked bacon (dark, crisp, glossy strips) on a white plate. Photographed from above, roughly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side plate). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 = 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Two or three pieces of cooked bacon, dark brown and crisp, with some rendered fat residue on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Bacon pieces together cover roughly 15% of the plate (about 47 cm^2). Fat residue under the pieces adds maybe 1%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon pile about 47 cm^2 x 0.5 cm (flat, folded pieces) = about 24 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 24 ml x 0.9 = about 21 g cooked bacon. Small rendered fat residue, about 1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon is roughly 540 kcal per 100 g (crisp, fat-rich). 21 g x 5.4 = about 113 kcal. Fat residue ~1 g x 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal (I'll keep it as a separate item).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two to three crisp bacon strips weigh about 15 to 25 g and provide roughly 100 to 130 kcal, which matches the visible amount.
